afd.text:

FXUS65 KPSR 250500
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1000 PM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather will persist through at least the weekend 
as temperatures gradually warm into a slightly above normal range. 

- Periods of breezy conditions over high terrain areas and along the 
lower Colorado River Valley will be common the next couple days. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
Early this afternoon upper level water vapor satellite imagery shows 
ridging across much of western CONUS with a shortwave trough over 
the western Pacific. The ridge currently overhead will lead to 
continued dry conditions and warming temperatures. As of early this 
afternoon, temperatures are around 2-6 degrees warmer than they were 
at the same time yesterday. Afternoon highs today are forecasted to 
be in the low to mid 70s  across the lower deserts and in the 60s 
across the higher terrain areas. Tomorrow, the aforementioned 
shortwave trough will quickly progress southwestward becoming a 
closed low over the Baja peninsula late Wednesday night. The system 
will miss our area to the south. Additionally, this will be a dry 
system and on top of the already dry airmass in place the Desert 
Southwest will see continued dry conditions. This system will just 
lead to breezy conditions across the Arizona high terrain in the 
morning and across southeast California, along with a period of semi-
thick higher level clouds Wednesday. Temperatures Wednesday will be 
similar, if not 1-2 degrees warmer, than today. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/... 
Near perfect weather is expected for Thanksgiving and through the 
holiday weekend as guidance heavily favors an upper level ridge 
building over the region and staying in place through at least 
Sunday. H5 heights are forecast to rise to between 582-585dm 
Thursday into Friday before leveling off over the weekend. This 
would place H5 heights well into the 90th percentile of climatology 
for late November, while NBM forecast highs rise into the upper 70s 
across the majority of the lower deserts starting Thursday. These 
highs of 5-8 degrees above normal should continue through the 
holiday weekend, while lows also warm to a few degrees above normal. 
Aside from the occasional passing high clouds, anticipate mostly 
clear skies through the period.

Model ensembles then point toward a large Pacific trough setting up 
off the West Coast Sunday into Monday before likely tracking through 
our region at some point around next Tuesday and/or Wednesday. 
Although still around a week away, models are leaning toward 
increased precipitation chances by the middle of next week, but so 
far it does not look like a very strong atmospheric river will 
impact the Desert Southwest.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0500Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Uncertainty and variability in wind direction will be the main 
weather concern through Wednesday night under frequent high cirrus 
decks. Confidence is good that an E/NE wind component will prevail 
the majority of the period, however large variability will be 
possible through the period. This includes a remote potential for 
the typical cold season counter-intuitive light SW wind at KPHX 
Wednesday morning, however odds are too low to include in this TAF 
package. Confidence is also low regarding wind directions late 
Wednesday afternoon as trajectories may attempt to become N/NW 
again, however may just remain E/NE through the entire late 
afternoon/evening. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather concerns will exist through Wednesday night under 
increasing high cirrus decks. Confidence is very good that winds 
will behave similarly to the past 24 hours, and generally vary 
between a west and north trajectory. Extended periods of nearly calm 
conditions will be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and tranquil conditions will continue across the region. 
Temperatures will warm to above normal by Thursday region wide and 
remain around 4-7 degrees above normal through the weekend. MinRH's 
will range between 15-30% through most of the forecast period, while 
cool overnight lows will result in decent to good overnight recovery 
each night. Outside of periods of marginally breezy conditions over 
AZ high terrain areas and the Lower Colorado River Valley (mainly 
today through Thursday), light winds will be favored.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Updated 11/23 1933Z.
Gila River: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to continued water releases upwards of 
3000 cfs. Water levels near Dateland continue to rise, with gauge 
data now showing a depth of just above 7 ft and flow exceeding 1100 
cfs. At the current rate of rise, the water level at the Dateland 
gauge is expected to reach action stage (8 ft) by Thursday-Friday. A 
separate Flood Warning segment remains in effect from Dateland to 
Yuma. These water levels will have the potential to flood farm 
fields and low water crossings along the river downstream from the 
dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Berislavich
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...18
FIRE WEATHER...Berislavich
HYDROLOGY...Benedict/RW
